title: Global Oil Markets – Executive Daily Brief
executive_summary: Markets are focused on freight and chokepoint risks around the Red Sea/Suez and Panama, tighter middle‑distillate balances at key hubs (ARA, Fujairah), and shifting Med flows as Iraq–Türkiye reopenings via Ceyhan scale unevenly. These dynamics tighten diesel/jet cracks in Northwest Europe, support East‑of‑Suez distillate spreads, and alter Atlantic–Pacific arbitrage economics for LNG/LPG and refined products.

developments.headline: Escalating Red Sea risk raises Suez transit premia and VLCC routing costs
developments.summary: A series of Houthi attacks this month—including the first deadly strike of 2026—has re‑elevated perceived risk for tankers transiting Bab el‑Mandeb/Suez. Analysts note operators are adjusting load volumes at Yanbu and using partial discharge at Ain Sukhna to meet Suez draught constraints, indicating more complex (and costlier) voyage planning. Expect wider war‑risk premia and some rerouting via the Cape for higher‑value cargoes or those with sensitive ownership profiles. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/29115cc1fbc209ed4be2d2f80eabc1bf?utm_source=openai))
developments.why_it_matters: Higher insurance and longer ton‑miles lift delivered crude and product costs into Europe and the Med, disproportionately impacting Jet A‑1/diesel supply chains into ARA/Med during peak demand windows; freight tightness can widen Med–NWE differentials and support cracks.

developments.headline: Ceyhan’s role grows as Iraq–Türkiye ink 1‑year pipeline deal, but actual flows remain subdued
developments.summary: Baghdad and Ankara agreed to a 1‑year arrangement enabling up to ~750 kb/d through the Kirkuk–Ceyhan corridor, positioning Ceyhan as a strategic alternative while Gulf routes face periodic disruption. However, reported Kirkuk‑to‑Ceyhan exports last week were closer to ~130 kb/d, underscoring that near‑term throughput depends on field, commercial, and political factors, not just capacity. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/f930588c201d6cb36c1cedb26a1f9331?utm_source=openai))
developments.why_it_matters: If sustained increases materialize, additional sour/medium barrels into the Med could pressure regional differentials (e.g., Urals alternatives, BTC blend interactions) and influence refinery slate choices in Türkiye/Italy/Spain; today, the gap between announced capacity and realized flows limits immediate price impact.

developments.headline: Middle‑distillate tightness emerges at key hubs: ARA gasoil draws; Fujairah stocks fall
developments.summary: Independent ARA data show gasoil inventories down ~9% m/m so far in August, with LSMGO prices up ~24% m/m, signaling tighter prompt barrels. In Fujairah, total product stocks fell ~9.9% w/w in the week to Aug 10, with middle distillates down 6%, per FOIZ‑based reporting. Together, these point to a firmer diesel/jet structure into late August. ([engine.online](https://www.engine.online/news/ara-fuel-oil-stocks-climb-10-pc-in-early-august-7f7b?utm_source=openai))
developments.why_it_matters: Tighter middle‑distillate availability supports diesel and jet cracks in NWE and East‑of‑Suez, narrows arbitrage from USGC when freight is elevated, and may pull incremental barrels from Med and Baltic, impacting barge and Rhine pricing transmission.

developments.headline: Panama Canal trims authorized draft to 48.5 ft (Aug 15), reshaping LNG/LPG and products arbitrage
developments.summary: ACP implemented a Neopanamax draft reduction to 48.5 ft effective Aug 15 as part of water‑management measures, following notices in July–August. While daily transit counts remain steady, reduced drafts raise per‑voyage costs and can favor Gulf‑to‑Europe over Gulf‑to‑Pacific flows for some products/LPG; LNG voyage economics to Asia weaken when combined with tepid arbitrage. ([agtransport.usda.gov](https://agtransport.usda.gov/stories/s/Transportation-Updates-and-Regulatory-News/wu88-46by/?utm_source=openai))
developments.why_it_matters: Shallower drafts can cap cargo size, increase slot competition and demurrage, and tilt USGC refined products and LPG toward Atlantic basins, tightening Asia‑bound arbitrage unless price spreads widen to offset freight and capacity constraints.

portfolio_implications: Favor long diesel/jet cracks in NWE vs gasoline near term; monitor ARA gasoil draws and Rhine/barge differentials for confirmation.
Maintain premium for Med delivery optionality; optional Ceyhan access could outperform if Iraqi/Türkiye volumes rise, but current low flows argue for patience.
For USGC‑to‑Asia flows (LPG/products), expect softer arbitrage unless Asia premiums/freight normalize; Atlantic‑focused placement strategies gain.
Freight exposure: consider higher war‑risk/insurance costs on Red Sea routes and potential Cape routings in risk scenarios.
risks: Rapid de‑escalation in Red Sea lowers premia and reverses recent crack support (downside to distillate length).
Unexpected Ceyhan throughput surge overwhelms Med cracks and differentials sooner than anticipated.
Panama hydrology improves and ACP restores higher drafts, reopening USGC‑to‑Pacific arbitrage earlier than modeled.
Demand shock (macro/FX) softens diesel uplift just as supply tightness peaks.
opportunities: Optionality in Med/NWE refinery runs and product placement to capture widening regional cracks.
Time‑charter or COA positions that benefit from elevated ton‑mile/Cape diversions.
Blending/quality arbitrage in ARA as middle‑distillate tightness elevates premiums for on‑spec LSMGO and jet.
Storage plays at Fujairah/ARA if backwardation eases on supply response.

FOIZ weekly update due next: confirm whether middle‑distillate draws persist into late August. ([foiz.gov.ae](https://foiz.gov.ae/statistics?utm_source=openai))
Ceyhan nominations and SOMO/KRG marketing updates; track realized exports vs announced capacity. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/f930588c201d6cb36c1cedb26a1f9331?utm_source=openai))
ACP advisories for any further draft/transit changes heading into September. ([pancanal.com](https://pancanal.com/en/maritime-services/notices-to-shipping/?utm_source=openai))

Insurance/warranty advisories for Red Sea transits; monitor MARAD/IMO updates and any new incidents. ([maritime.dot.gov](https://www.maritime.dot.gov/msci/2026-006-red-sea-bab-el-mandeb-strait-gulf-aden-arabian-sea-and-somali-basin-houthi-attacks?utm_source=openai))
